This is the complaint instituted by the complainant against the accused under Section 200 Cr.P.C. for the offence punishable under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act1881.
2.

The Case of the complainant as per complaint averments is as follows:
The complainant is a company registered under the companies Act, 1956 carrying on the business of vehicle finance and engaged in the business of extending finance facility to its customers.
The accused approached the SCCH-10 complainant company and availed the vehicle loan of Rs.3,56,619/ on 30.04.2013 for purchase of ACE Mini LCV vehicle under under Loan A/c No.XVFPVG000000963280.
The accused has agreed to repay the loan amount in monthly installments.
The accused has failed to repay the loan dues.
The complainant repossessed the vehicle and disposed the same.
On adjusting the sale proceeds, the accused was due a sum of Rs.1,50,414/ to the complainant company.
After repeated request, in discharge of his liability, the accused has issued a cheque bearing No.007494 dated 07.10.2016 for a sum of Rs.1,50,414/ drawn on Union Bank of India, Devanahalli Branch.

The said cheque was presented by the complainant through its banker ICICI Bank, Bommanahalli Branch, Bengaluru, but the same has been returned with an endorsement "Account blocked" as per the bankers memo dated 25.10.2016.

Then, the complainant got issued a legal notice to the accused dated 18.11.2016, calling upon him to pay the cheque amount within 15 days from the date of SCCH-10 receipt and the said notice was returned unserved on 26.11.2016.
In spite of issuance of notice, the accused has not paid the cheque amount.
Thus, the accused has committed the offence punishable U/Sec.138 of Negotiable Instruments Act.
Hence, this complaint.
3. After filing of the complaint, the cognizance of the offence was taken and registered criminal case against the accused and the summons was issued to him.
Upon service of the summons, the accused has appeared before the Court through his counsel and was enlarged on bail.
Subsequently, plea was recorded and the substance of the accusation was read over and explained to him.
He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
Then, the case was posted for complainant evidence.

4. In view of the judgment rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Indian Bank Association and others V/s. Union of India and others  (2014) 5 SCC 590, the sworn statement on affidavit of complainant is treated as SCCH-10 examinationinchief and the documents produced M/S.Cholamandalam Investment And ... vs Babu P N on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22348335/
2 by the complainant were marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.6.
5.

6. Heard the arguments.
Perused the materials available on record.

7. Now the points that arise for my determination are as follows:
1) Whether the complainant proved that the accused has committed an offence punishable u/s 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act?
2) What order?
8.

On the basis of the materials available on record, my finding to the above points are as follows:
 POINT NO.1: In the Affirmative.
 SCCH-10  POINT NO.2: As per the final order,
 for the following:
 REASONS 9. POINT NO.1: I have gone through the entire materials available on record.
According to the complainant, the accused approached the complainant company for financial assistance for purchase of vehicle.
Based on the request of the accused, the complainant company sanctioned the loan amount of Rs.3,56,619/ under Loan A/c No.XVFPVG000000963280, which the accused required to repay monthly installments.

It is the further case of the complainant that, the accused failed to repay the installment and the complainant has repossessed the vehicle and disposed the same and after adjusting the sale proceeds, the accused is liable to pay a sum of Rs.1,50,414/ and in discharge of his liability, the accused has issued a cheque bearing No.007494, dated:07.10.2016 for a sum of Rs.1,50,414/ drawn on Union Bank of India, Devanahalli Branch and when the said cheque was SCCH-10 presented, same was dishonoured with an endorsement "Account Blocked" as per the banker's memo dated 25.10.2016.
Further, the complainant got issued a legal notice to the accused calling upon him to pay the cheque amount within 15 days from the date of receipt of the said notice.
In spite of issuance of notice, the accused has not paid the cheque amount.
10. To substantiate its case, the Authorized signatory of the complainant company was examined as PW1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.6.

The PW1 has reiterated the contents of the complaint in his affidavit evidence about lending of loan to the accused for purchase of vehicle, issuance of cheque by the accused towards discharge of his liability and its dishonour and issuance of the legal notice to M/S.Cholamandalam Investment And ... vs Babu P N on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22348335/

11. In this scenario, let me scrutinize the documents relied by the complainant in order to examine the compliance of statutory requirements as envisaged under SCCH-10 Section 138 of N.I. Act,

The Ex.P.1 is the copy of GPA, Ex.P.2 the is the Cheque dated 07.10.2016, the Ex.P.2(a) is the signature of the accused and the said cheque was returned with an endorsement "Account Blocked" as per Ex.P.3 bank endorsement dated 25.10.2016.
Ex.P.4 is the legal notice dated 18.11.2016, Ex.P.5 is postal receipt, Ex.P.6 is the unserved postal cover and Ex.P.6(a) is the copy of Legal notice.
On careful perusal of the documents relied by the complainant goes to show that, statutory requirements of Section 138 of N.I. Act is complied with and this complaint is filed within time.
Further the complainant has discharged his initial burden by relying oral and documentary evidence.

Thus, the complainant is entitled to rely on the statutory presumptions enshrined under Section 118 read with Section 139 of N.I. Act.
12.

As far as proof of existence of legally enforceable debt is concerned, it is profitable to refer the decision of full bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in Rangappa Vs. SCCH-10 Mohan reported in AIR 2010 SC 1898, wherein their lordships pleased to observe that, "In the light of these extracts, we are in agreement with the respondentclaimant that the presumption mandated by Section 139 of the Act does indeed include the existence of the legally enforceable debt or liability".

entities.text: Rangappa Vs. SCCH-10 Mohan reported in AIR 2010 SC 1898
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
13. In another decision reported in, (2015) 8 SCC 378 in the case of Vasanthakumar Vs.
Vijayakumari, it is held that once the accused has admitted the issuance of Cheque as well as signature on it, the presumption under Section 139 would be attracted.
In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, the presumption enshrined under Section 139 of the N.I. Act is extendable to the existence of legally enforceable debt.
The Hon'ble Apex Court has clearly laid down the ratio that, when the ingredients of Section 138 of NI Act are complied with, presumption shall be drawn in favour of the complainant.
The burden is upon the accused to rebut the statutory presumptions.
In the SCCH-10 instant case the accused neither crossexamined PW1 nor lead any evidence to rebut the said presumption.

14. In the decision reported in, AIR 2019 Supreme Court 1876, in the case Rohitbhai Jivanlal Patel Vs. State of Gujarat and Another; wherein it is held that, "once presumption of existence of legally enforceable debt drawn in favour of complainant, onus is shifted on accused Unless onus is discharged by accused that preponderance of probabilities are tilting in his favour, doubt on case of complainant cannot be raised for want of evidence regarding source of funds for advancing loan to accused."
15.

entities.text: Rohitbhai Jivanlal Patel Vs. State of Gujarat and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: From the above proposition of law it is now trite that presumptions available under Section 139 and 118 of NI Act are rebuttable in nature.
The accused can take probable defence in the scale of preponderance of probability to rebut the presumption available to the complainant.
Let me examine whether the accused has successfully rebutted the said presumptions of law.
I have SCCH-10 given anxious consideration to the materials available on record.

At the outset, the accused has not disputed issuance of cheque and his signature in the cheque by way of crossexamination or M/S.Cholamandalam Investment And ... vs Babu P N on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22348335/
4 by leading defence evidence.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It goes without saying that, accused has not disputed the cheques in question and signatures found therein.

When the drawer has admitted the issuance of the cheque as well as the signature present therein, the presumptions as envisaged under Section 118 read with Section 139 of NI Act, would operate in favour of the complainant.
16. It is worth to note that, Section 106 of Indian Evidence Act postulates that, the burden is on the accused to establish the fact which is especially within his special knowledge.
This provision is exception to the General Rule that, the burden of proof is always on the prosecution to establish their case beyond all reasonable doubt.
In that view of the matter, the burden is on the accused to prove SCCH-10 that the cheque in question not issued for discharge of any liability.
17. In order to prove his case, the complainant examined himself as PW1 by reiterating the contents of the complaint and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P6.
Despite of giving sufficient time, the accused did not even crossexamine PW1.
Therefore, the evidence placed by the complainant is remained unchallenged and there is no reason to disbelieve the version of the complainant.
Though the accused has denied the transaction while recording of his plea, but in support of his defence he has neither crossexamined PW1 nor led any defence evidence.
The accused has completely failed to rebut the presumption.
Hence, the presumption available in favour of the complainant under Section 139 and 118 of NI Act remained unrebutted.

Accordingly the complainant has proved that,
for discharge of liability accused has issued Ex.P.2 cheque and he has intentionally not maintained sufficient amount in his account to honour SCCH-10 the said cheque.
Hence, this Point No.1 under consideration is answered in the Affirmative.
18. POINT NO.2:

In view of the reasons stated and discussed above, the complainant has proved that the accused has committed an offence punishable under Section 138 of N.I. Act.
19.

Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in a decision reported in (2015) 17 SCC 368, in a case of H.Pukhraj Vs. D.Parasmal, observed that, having regard to the length of trial and date of issuance of the cheque, it is necessary to award reasonable interest on the cheque amount along with cost of litigation.

Therefore, keeping in mind the time when the transaction has taken place and primary object of the provision, this court is of the opinion that, rather than imposing punitive sentence, if sentence of fine is imposed with a direction to compensate the complainant for his monitory loss, by awarding compensation U/Sec.357 of Cr.P.C, would meet the ends of justice.
By keeping in mind SCCH-10 Sec.143(1), Sec.80 and 117 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, the compensation has to be awarded.
20 . As per the records, the transaction was taken place in the year 2013 and the cheque was dated 07.10.2016 and amount covered under said cheque is Rs.1,50,414/.
It appears that, the complainant has spent considerable time and money to prosecute the case.

By considering all these aspects, this court is of the opinion that, it is just and proper to impose fine amount of Rs.1,60,000/, which includes interest and cost of litigation, out of which compensation of Rs.1,58,000/ has to be awarded to the complainant U/s 357 Cr.P.C.

Accordingly, this court M/S.Cholamandalam Investment And ... vs Babu P N on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22348335/

sentences.text: ORDER Acting under Sec. 255(2) of Cr.P.C., the accused is found guilty and he is convicted for the offence punishable under Section 138 of Negotiable Instruments Act and he is sentenced to pay a fine of Rs.1,60,000/ (Rupees One lakh Sixty Thousand only).
In default to pay the fine, SCCH-10 accused shall undergo simple imprisonment for a period of six months.

Further, acting under Sec.357(1)(b) of Cr.P.C., a sum of Rs.1,58,000/ (Rupees One lakh Fifty Eight Thousand only) on recovery shall be paid to the complainant as compensation and Rs.2,000/ shall be remitted to the state exchequer for the expenses incurred for prosecution.
Supply free copy of this judgment to the accused immediately.
The bail bond stands canceled.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer, typed by her and corrected by me and then pronounced in the open Court on 14 th day of June 2024).
(RAGHAVENDRA SHETTIGAR) XIV ADDL.S.C.J., ACMM & MEMBERMACT, BENGALURU.
